messages:
mira: Heads-up — after yesterday's RBAC change + scheduled KMS rotation we're seeing a burst of SAST regressions in CI for payment-service. Alert window ~09:02 UTC. Looks noisy but affects multiple PRs. Any leads?

sec-bot: Automated scan summary: 23 failures across policy set 'sast-v2', top rule ids: SND-102, SND-210. Scanner v1.4.2. See logs: https://ci.internal/reports/3456789012 (redacted tokens).

jon: Can you paste the failing rule excerpts? Also checking if scanner image changed during rotation. infra didn't touch scanner images but we rotated KMS keys for blob store.

sam: Failing snippet (from one of the CI attachments):

```
file: services/payment/gen/payment_pb2.py
line: 87
issue: SND-102 - possible SQL concatenation pattern detected in formatted string
code: "cursor.execute(f\"INSERT INTO tx ({cols}) VALUES ({vals})\")"
```

sam: This looks like generated protobuf wrapper code introducing a debug helper that builds SQL-like strings for tests. Definitely suspicious as a FP.

leo: I ran the scanner locally against the same commit hash — same hits. Repro steps: `docker run --rm -v $PWD:/src redwood/scanner:1.4.2 scan /src --rules sast-v2 --format json > out.json`. The generated file is in `gen/` and scanner flags it.

mira: Could KMS rotation or RBAC change influence scan results? I wouldn't expect scan findings to change because of KMS, unless build artifacts changed (different codegen or stripped metadata). Anything in the build pipeline that pulls secrets?

jon: KMS rotation only replaced decryption keys for artifact signing; artifacts should be identical. However, we also changed a service account policy which removed a read permission from the codegen service for an internal template store — that could cause fallback to a local generator with different output.

sam: Good catch. If template store read failed, codegen may have emitted a fallback helper with string interpolation. That explains generated SQL-like helpers.

mira: Action items: 1) sam to triage and confirm generated vs canonical output; 2) jon to validate service account permission change and restore if necessary; 3) leo to gather evidence and make suppression proposal if FP. Assign owners and ETA? :calendar:

sam: I'll take triage (starting now). Plan: reproduce canonical generation by running codegen with service account token, compare diffs, and run scanner. ETA 60m. @jon ping me when you check the SA change.

jon: I'm rolling back the SA change in a dev-only path to verify. Will update in 15m.

leo: Evidence attached to the CI alert: diff of generated files + scan JSON. If we decide suppression, I'll open a suppression PR with evidence and unit test to catch future regressions.

mira: If it's generated code we should not block merges — create suppression with clear rationale. Also add a premerge heuristic to ignore `gen/` patterns for this rule family. File an issue for the policy change.

sec-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-847 - "SAST regression spike after RBAC change". Tags: sast, oncall, false-positive-potential. Link: https://incidents.internal/847

sam: Quick update — reproduced locally with service account absent; codegen emits extra helper. With proper token it emits compact helpers that don't include SQL-like f-strings. Confirmed root cause is permission fallback.

jon: Restored read permission for codegen SA in staging. Will promote to prod after validation.

sam: Re-ran scanner against artifacts produced with restored SA — all SND-102 hits gone.

leo: I'll open suppression PR for the handful of false positives that slipped into historic branches, include diffs and CI attachments. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/3424

mira: Good work. Follow-ups: (a) write a short postmortem in #postmortems describing the RBAC -> codegen fallback coupling, (b) extend premerge rule exceptions for generated dirs, (c) add a check in the deploy playbook to verify codegen SA perms before KMS rotations.

sam: I'll draft the postmortem and the suppression PR description. Leaving this thread open until PR merges and prod validation completes.

mira: Thanks all — marking as assigned. If anything else pops up, ping here. :thumbsup:
